sources.title: California DIR General Prevailing Wage Determinations (journeyman) - 2026-2 edition (statewide, Northern California, Southern California, San Diego, subtrades, shift differentials)
sources.owner: California Department of Industrial Relations (DIR), Director's Office - Research Unit (URL path /oprl/)
sources.data_provided: Per-craft, per-region general prevailing wage determinations: basic hourly rate, fringe components (health and welfare, pension, vacation and holiday, training, other payments), total hourly rate, overtime/holiday multipliers in footnotes, and expiration with predetermined-increase flags.

sources.period_covered: 2026-2 edition current as of 2026-10 (inferred from 2026-2 index/notice pages existing); each determination has its own expiration date
sources.edition: 2026-2 (prior editions 2026-1, 2025-2, 2025-1 ... 2016-1 remain online under the same pattern)
sources.access_notes: HTML index pages by region plus one PDF per craft/area, e.g. https://www.dir.ca.gov/oprl/2025-2/PWD/Determinations/Southern/SC-023-31-2.pdf (Carpenter and related trades, Southern). Predetermined wage-increase PDFs/HTML live under .../PWD/Increases/Southern/SC-023-31-2-Pre.pdf and .../Increases/Subtrades/LOS-Pre.html. Full determination number pattern seen: SC-23-31-2-2025-2 (region-craft-?-?-edition); San Diego pattern SD-23-102-4-2026-1. A statewide craft listing page pattern is .../PWD/C-Driver-List.htm. The 2026-2 carpenter PDF was NOT returned by search, only the 2025-2 version; its URL is a derived pattern. No API or bulk/CSV/Excel download was found in results. One 2023 PDF snippet showed headers but no rate table in the indexed text (possible text-extraction problem to plan for); the document told users to request rates from the Research Unit at (415) 703-4774.
sources.reuse_terms: No reuse/copyright statement for DIR determinations appeared in results. State agency public records; terms must be checked on dir.ca.gov before bulk republication.
sources.limitations: Prevailing wage applies to public works (and other covered work) - it is a union-scale-driven legal minimum, not the market wage of a non-union crew and not a total loaded cost. Rates change on predetermined schedules mid-edition (e.g. increase on July 1) and are changed by correction/modification notices between editions. Travel and subsistence is governed separately (Labor Code 1773.1, 1773.9 per boilerplate) and is not a single published figure in the determination. Consumer must apply the correct area, effective date and increase tables.
sources.update_frequency: Twice a year (issued February 22 and August 22 per DIR FAQ snippet), effective 10 days after issuance, plus ad hoc modification/correction notices and predetermined increases
sources.evidence_quote: The index pages set out a six-step lookup. Step one checks statewide basic trades, step two checks the Northern and Southern California basic trades, step three covers San Diego County, step four covers county subtrades, step five covers shift differentials, and step six covers notices of corrections or modifications.

findings.topic: California DIR general prevailing wage determinations: publication cycle
findings.statement: General determinations are issued twice a year (February 22 and August 22) and become effective 10 days after issuance; they remain in effect until their expiration date or until modified, corrected, rescinded or superseded. Editions are published in folders named YYYY-1 and YYYY-2 (e.g. 2026-1, 2026-2) with HTML index pages and per-craft PDFs. Between editions DIR issues modification/correction notices (e.g. Aug 27 2026 plumber modification; Sep 3 2026 apprentice painter correction) and predetermined-increase files. A single asterisk after the expiration date means rates in effect when bids are advertised remain for the life of the project; double asterisk means post-expiration rates are predetermined.

findings.topic: California DIR determination structure, numbering, formats and access
findings.statement: Format is PDF per craft/area under .../oprl/{YYYY}-{1|2}/PWD/Determinations/{Southern|Northern|SanDiego|Statewide}/ with file names like SC-023-31-2.pdf and a full determination number like SC-23-31-2-2025-2 (Southern California, craft 23, then -31-2-edition), SD-23-102-4-2026-1 for San Diego, SC-102-507-1 for housemovers. Contents: basic hourly rate and fringe columns (health and welfare, pension, vacation and holiday, training, other payments), an overtime group code and total hourly rate (structure seen in the 2021 carpenter PDF), with overtime/holiday multipliers in footnotes (examples seen: daily/Saturday 1.5x, Sunday/holiday 2x, hours over 12 per day at Sunday/holiday rate). Travel and subsistence is covered by boilerplate referring to Labor Code 1773.1 and 1773.9, not by a rate table in the snippets. No API, CSV or bulk download was found; one DIR PDF told users to request determinations from the Research Unit by phone. Rates for 2026 carpenter (SC-23-31-2) were not retrieved; only the 2025-2 version (issued Aug 22 2025, expiring Jun 30 2026) and the 2025-1 predetermined increase file were seen.
findings.evidence_quote: The 2026-2 index page lists Carpenter as a craft with a predetermined increase, but the search didn't return the SC-023-31-2 PDF for that cycle.

findings.topic: California EDD OEWS-based wage tables are published but are an aged derivative
findings.statement: EDD LMI publishes Excel files by geographic area, an OEWS dashboard and a wages search tool; multi-county MSAs are disaggregated into single metropolitan-division datasets (county-level for Los Angeles County). As indexed, wages are aged to Q1 2025 using the ECI on the 2018 SOC wage database with May 2024 employment, so EDD's tables lag the BLS May 2025 release and are not identical to BLS values. Percentiles shown are 25/50/75. Terms of use were not found.
findings.evidence_quote: The EDD also disaggregated occupational employment and wage data for multi-county MSAs into single MD datasets annually, which gives county-level detail for multi-county metros.

findings.topic: SAM.gov Davis-Bacon wage determinations: location, formats, API
findings.statement: DOL moved Wage Determinations OnLine to SAM.gov on June 14, 2019 and WDOL.gov is retired. Davis-Bacon general determinations are issued for four construction types (building, residential, highway, heavy - heavy is the catch-all) and are county-based; users filter by state, county and type and can download .txt or print to PDF; each WD has a modification history and a SAM.gov account is needed to follow a WD for alerts. 'Residential' covers single-family houses or apartment buildings of no more than four stories (per a DOL-derived guide). Annual rollover editions are issued in the first quarter. No official API or API key requirement for wage determinations was found; a third-party tool says rates are only plain text and relies on an undocumented internal web endpoint with no county filter. Treat any automated ingest as unconfirmed until api.sam.gov / open.gsa.gov documentation is read.
findings.evidence_quote: One MCP server's documentation says it parses rates from plain-text wage determination documents because SAM exposes no structured rate JSON.

findings.topic: Davis-Bacon general determinations covering Southern California (what was seen)
findings.statement: A 2026 California GD (CA20260029 Rev 1, Alpine/Amador/Calaveras etc.) was listed by a third-party aggregator (bidpulsar), which shows the numbering pattern CA2026nnnn but is not Los Angeles. An archived Los Angeles copy hosted by the U.S. District Court is titled 'Davis-Bacon Act WD#CA20200022 (Los Angeles)' while the search tool described it as CA20240022 dated 11/08/2024 - the identifier/date is inconsistent and unverified. The current Los Angeles County building/residential/heavy/highway GD numbers and revisions were NOT established.
findings.evidence_quote: dba ca20260029 r1

findings.topic: Nevada prevailing wage regime and publication
findings.statement: Nevada has a state public-works prevailing wage regime administered by the Labor Commissioner under NRS 338, with four prevailing wage regions (Clark County Region established by NRS 338.025; a Northern Nevada Rural Region also seen) published as PDFs on labor.nv.gov with numbered amendments. The Clark County 2025-2026 determination applied to public works over $100,000 bid/awarded Oct 1, 2025 - Sep 30, 2026; amendments continued to at least 6/24/26. The successor determination (Oct 1, 2026) was not found by search. Objections must be filed within 30 days of issuance.
findings.evidence_quote: The determination cites NRS 338.025, which establishes the Clark Prevailing Wage Region consisting of Clark County, one of four state regions.

findings.topic: Arizona prevailing wage regime (unresolved; no official source)
findings.statement: Per contractor/marketing pages (tier E), Arizona has no general state prevailing-wage statute for public works and Davis-Bacon applies to federally funded work; one such page says Arizona law prohibits state and local agencies from requiring prevailing wage in public works contracts, while a contractor-association page claims A.R.S. 34-321 applies to state-funded construction with Department of Administration determinations - these conflict and neither is official. The only official source found is the Arizona Attorney General Opinion I23-004 about Phoenix's ordinance (prevailing wages on city contracts over $250,000, referencing Davis-Bacon rates). Treat Arizona prevailing wage as unconfirmed pending statute text (A.R.S. Title 34) and AG opinion read-through.
findings.evidence_quote: One contractor association guide says § 34-321 applies to state-funded public works construction contracts, with wage determinations issued by the Arizona Department of Administration. That contradicts the other sources, and I could not verify the statute from these results.

findings.topic: Employer burden: federal and California percentage items (kept separate from wages and fringes)
findings.statement: FICA employer share 2026: Social Security 6.2% up to a $184,500 wage base; Medicare 1.45% no cap (IRS Pub 15 2026 text via search summary). FUTA: 6.0% on first $7,000 with up to 5.4% credit giving 0.6% net - seen only on a secondary site; California credit-reduction status needs the Form 940 instructions. California EDD 2026: ETT 0.1% on first $7,000; UI Schedule F+ range 1.5% to 6.2% on first $7,000, employer-specific rate on DE 2088; SDI 1.3% is an employee withholding (employee-paid) with no wage cap - so exclude from employer burden. A 3.4% new-employer UI rate was claimed only by a payroll blog and was not found on EDD's page.
findings.evidence_quote: EDD lists the 2026 withholding rate as 1.3%, and all wages are subject to SDI contributions with no wage cap.

findings.topic: California workers' compensation: class codes and what is public
findings.statement: WCIRB Classification Search publishes phraseologies, footnotes, rules and approved advisory pure premium rates by class. Confirmed class pairs (low-wage/high-wage dual classes): 5403/5432 Carpentry, 5183(1)/5187(1) Plumbing, 5190/5140 Electrical Wiring. Dual-wage thresholds (Sept 1, 2024): plumbing 32, electrical 36, carpentry 41 USD per hour; a Nov 2025 committee deck proposed electrical 40 but adoption was not confirmed. The WCIRB dual-wage PDF title lists class numbers 5027 5140 5183 5185 5201 5403 5446 5467 5474 5484 5538 5552 5630 5632 5645 6218; likely descriptions from prior knowledge (UNVERIFIED): 5201 concrete/cement work, 5446 wallboard installation, 5474 painting, 5538 sheet metal work, 5552 roofing, 5645 residential carpentry, 5185 automatic sprinkler installation. HVAC is said to share the plumbing 5183/5187 split per search summary. Published rates are advisory pure premiums (average $1.65 per $100 payroll effective 9/1/2026); insurers file their own rates and experience modification is company-specific, so actual comp cost must come from the company's policy/audit, not WCIRB. Multi-state class lists (Tennessee, Amerisafe, Nevada assigned-risk) were seen but are not California authority and were ignored.
findings.evidence_quote: The adopted rate is advisory, meaning that insurance companies are not bound by it and are free to set their own rates.

findings.topic: Third-party salary pages seen but deliberately not used
findings.statement: Pages from tradecareerpath.com, wagedex.com, miter.com, workyard.com, ebacon.com, payroll4construction.com, ontheclock.com, mercury.com, beancount.io and glama.ai appeared. They carry OEWS-derived or prevailing-wage numbers (e.g. LA-area carpenter annual wages, a $88.52 Clark County average journeyman rate) but are tier E and official sources exist; no wage numbers from them were recorded as data points.
findings.evidence_quote: A salary page lists the Los Angeles-Long Beach-Anaheim metro with 30,600 employed, a median annual wage of $75,740, an average annual wage of $78,600

gaps: No official OEWS detailed-occupation wage for any construction trade in the Los Angeles-Long Beach-Glendale metropolitan division (or Riverside-San Bernardino-Ontario, Phoenix, Las Vegas) was retrievable: the search tool never returned the XLSX/table content. Needed: fetch the May 2025 MSA/MD XLSX from bls.gov (blocked in this sandbox) and read the actual rows for SOC 47-2031 etc.

Exact May 2025 OEWS data-file names and URLs (national/state/metro ZIP or XLSX), the column header list and the CBSA codes for the four metros: not confirmed; prior-knowledge guesses are flagged. Need the bls.gov/oes/tables.htm page or a directory listing.
Whether the May 2025 OEWS tables publish the Los Angeles-Long Beach-Glendale metropolitan division separately from the MSA: not confirmed.
Official BLS statement of the exact OEWS benefit-exclusion wording and the OEWS FAQ page text were not read; only the search-tool summary of the technical notes was seen.
Full OEWS series-ID layout and datatype codes: only field-width fragments seen; need oe.txt and oe.datatype. No OEWS series ID is reported.

ECEC: no construction-industry series ID seen; BLS's own construction table values (as opposed to EPI's reproduction) not seen; latest ECEC quarter as of Oct 2026 unknown (Dec 2025 was the one seen); regional (West) ECEC availability not established.
ECI regional/metro cuts (West region, Los Angeles) and a trade-specific cut were not searched beyond the national construction series.

PPI: gypsum (WPU137 vs other), asphalt roofing, paint, copper wire/pipe and 'inputs to construction industries' IDs came only via search-tool summaries of AGC tables; the BLS PPI series lookup should be used to validate each ID, title and base period. WPUID611 not confirmed.
FRED numeric rate limits and the exact FRED legal statement about BLS data were not seen; legal review needed before any storage of FRED-sourced data.

California DIR: current 2026-2 (and 2026-1) Southern California determination rate tables were not retrieved for any craft; effective dates, predetermined increases and the exact 2026 carpenter, laborer, electrician, plumber, painter, drywall, operating engineer rates are unknown. The meaning of the numeric components of the determination number (e.g. 23-31-2) is not documented in snippets. DIR terms of use for republication were not found. No API/bulk download found; need to confirm by reading the DIR PWD index page and the OPRL pages.
Whether DIR travel-and-subsistence (zones/per diem) is published as numbers anywhere in the determinations or in separate zone pages was not established.

SAM.gov: no official API documentation for wage determinations found (open.gsa.gov / api.sam.gov); current Los Angeles County DBA general decision numbers, revisions and the Arizona and Nevada county decisions were not retrieved; the Los Angeles court-hosted copy has an inconsistent identifier (CA20200022 in title vs CA20240022 in summary).
Arizona: no official statute text or state agency page confirming whether a state prevailing-wage regime exists; conflicting contractor claims about A.R.S. 34-321.

Nevada: the October 1, 2026 successor determinations (Clark County and other regions) and the labor.nv.gov landing page were not seen; the Northern Nevada and other region names/URL patterns beyond those listed are not confirmed.

EDD OEWS: Excel file URLs and column layout not seen; current vintage (page may have moved beyond the aged-to-Q1-2025 version); no terms of use found; other EDD labor-market series (e.g. Employment Projections) not searched.

FUTA from IRS primary source (Form 940 instructions) and California's FUTA credit-reduction status for 2026 not checked; EDD's own statement of new-employer UI rate not found; EDD explicit statement that SDI is employee-paid not read (inferred from 'withholding rate' wording).

WCIRB: California class-code descriptions for drywall, painting, concrete, HVAC, roofing, glazing, sheet metal, insulation and rebar were not confirmed from WCIRB pages; class-level advisory pure premium rates for 9/1/2026 were not seen; WCIRB free-vs-paid access boundaries (e.g. rating data, experience rating worksheet) not established.

Nothing was searched for Arizona/Nevada employer-burden items (state UI/workers comp: Nevada and Arizona SUI rates, NCCI states) or for local/other benefit contribution rates (union trust fund rates, apprenticeship) outside the DIR determinations.
blocked_or_unverifiable: The search tool returns an AI-written summary with some quoted fragments, not raw page text or HTML snippets. All evidence_quote values are copied literally from that returned summary text and may paraphrase the underlying pages; none were checked against the actual page content.

bls.gov, dir.ca.gov, sam.gov, dol.gov, irs.gov data/page fetches are blocked in the sandbox (per brief), so no URL listed here was fetched; the .zip/.xlsx file names for OEWS May 2025 and the BLS API endpoint URL cannot be verified.

Prior-knowledge items (verification_method prior_knowledge_unverified): oesm25*.zip names and /oes/special-requests/ path; OEWS column names; CBSA codes; SOC code titles for all 14 requested trades; BLS API endpoint https://api.bls.gov/publicAPI/v2/timeseries/data/; WCIRB class descriptions beyond 5403/5432, 5183/5187, 5190/5140; statement that federal government works are generally public domain; expected next OEWS release timing.

Several figures reached only via tier-E pages: FUTA 6.0%/5.4%/0.6% (ustax.tools), new-employer UI rate 3.4% (ontheclock.com), Miter's $88.52 Clark County average rate, third-party carpenter wage tables, bidpulsar DBA listing. None of these should be used as authoritative inputs.

The Davis-Bacon 2,000 USD contract-value coverage threshold was stated in the search summary of Arizona results but could not be tied to a specific result URL (contractor/marketing pages mixed in), so it is not recorded as a data point; confirm from DOL.
The CA20260017 Rev 3 'Imperial, Los Angeles, Orange +5' Davis-Bacon listing mentioned by the search tool could not be tied to a specific result URL, so it is not recorded.

The search tool noted internal inconsistencies it could not resolve: ECEC seasonal-adjustment code differs between the ECEC and ECI copies of the guide; DIR 2026-1 vs 2026-2 index/notice labelling; CA court-hosted DBA PDF identifier. These remain open until the live pages are read.
